subject: physical-education

location.unitTitle: Fitness Literacy II: Designing a Personal Program

standardsMappingAuthority.note: Standards remain governed by the bound production package.

instructions: Complete the safe activity or accessible equivalent and document the requested performance evidence.
Stop for pain, dizziness, breathing trouble, unsafe conditions, or missing adult supervision.

learnerTasks.prompt: Explain the critical features or key principle of setting a capability goal that is specific and testable by task in your own words.
Demonstrate or fully describe building a weekly structure around real constraints using a version your body and setting allow. A described or adapted version earns full credit.
Apply sequencing sessions and balancing hard and easy days in a new situation and explain the decision or adjustment you made.
Analyze a plausible technique fault, tactical error, or unsafe choice involving progressing safely and recognizing when to hold; correct it and explain why.
Connect adherence: what makes a program survive a bad week with reviewing and revising a program mid-cycle and explain how one affects the other.
Present the strongest evidence from the unit task: Write, run, and review a six-week personal program built around a self-chosen capability goal, documenting one mid-cycle revision and its reason.
Identify one thing you can now do or direct yourself, one adjustment that improved it, and one next goal you set for yourself.

learnerSuccessCriteria: Provide evidence that meets the stated safe participation and self-management criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated skill cues or movement quality criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated tactical or training reasoning criterion.
Provide evidence that meets the stated self-assessment and revision criterion.
accommodations: Access supports may change format, pacing, intensity, range, equipment, setting, or response mode without changing the standard being assessed. An adapted or described performance is full credit, not partial credit.

provenance.unitObjective: How can the learner demonstrate the goals of Fitness Literacy II: Designing a Personal Program?
